chunks: 1675 - Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated; he said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about women—how the jizyah was dropped and lifted from them. So he said:

“Because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade the killing of women and children in Dār al-Ḥarb, unless they fight. And even if she fights as well, then refrain from her as much as you can, so long as you do not fear a breach.

So when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله forbade killing them in Dār al-Ḥarb, that was even more fitting in Dār al-Islām. And if she were to refuse to pay the jizyah, her killing would not be possible; so when her killing was not possible, the jizyah was lifted from her.

But if the men withheld and refused to pay the jizyah, they would be breaking the covenant, and their blood and their killing would become lawful, because killing men is permissible in Dār al-Shirk and in the case of dhimmah.
And likewise, the crippled among the people of shirk and dhimmah, the blind, the aged old man, the woman, and the children in the land of war—for that reason, the jizyah was lifted from them.”

key_terms.الذِّمَّةِ: Protected covenantal status granted to non-Muslims under Muslim rule.
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةُ: The poll tax taken from certain non-Muslim subjects under Islamic rule.
key_terms.الْمُقْعَدُ: A physically disabled or crippled person.
key_terms.دَارِ الْإِسْلَامِ: The domain of Islam; territory under Muslim rule.
key_terms.دَارِ الْحَرْبِ: The domain of war; territory outside Muslim rule in a state of hostility.
key_terms.نَاقِضِينَ لِلْعَهْدِ: Those breaking the covenant or pact.

ai.seo_question: Why are women and other vulnerable non-Muslims exempt from jizyah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal reasoning for exempting women and certain vulnerable groups from jizyah. The Imam عليه السلام grounds the ruling in the Prophetic prohibition against killing women and children in war, arguing that where killing is not lawful for refusal, jizyah is not imposed.
